findings.claim: A quarter of sessions (30-minute gap) consist of a single game; the median session has 3 games and 7% of sessions reach 10 or more games.
findings.metric: share of sessions with exactly one game
findings.caveat: Sessions recomputed over standard live games only (53 games change position relative to the stored session column); 14% of games sit in a session that mixes time classes.

findings.claim: Bullet sessions are the long ones: 44% have five or more games and 14% ten or more, against 19% and 2% for blitz.
findings.metric: share of bullet-dominated sessions with at least 5 games
findings.caveat: Sessions classified by their main time class.

findings.claim: A loss ends the session about a third of the time and a win about a sixth, so the last game of every session is selected to be a bad one.
findings.metric: P(game is the last of its session | loss), with difference P(stop | loss) - P(stop | win); P(stop | win) = 0.173 [0.160, 0.187]
findings.caveat: This selection bends every naive curve by game number: late games are over-represented by losses and look like fatigue.

findings.claim: In bullet a loss ends the session 29% of the time and a win 11%.
findings.metric: P(stop | loss), with difference P(stop | loss) - P(stop | win); P(stop | win) = 0.114 [0.099, 0.129]

findings.claim: In blitz a loss ends the session 38% of the time and a win 25%.
findings.metric: P(stop | loss), with difference P(stop | loss) - P(stop | win); P(stop | win) = 0.254 [0.226, 0.282]

findings.claim: In rapid a loss ends the session 42% of the time and a win 24%.
findings.metric: P(stop | loss), with difference P(stop | loss) - P(stop | win); P(stop | win) = 0.243 [0.194, 0.293]

findings.claim: The player already stops more often after two losses in a row (0.353) than after two wins in a row (0.143), and more than after a single loss.
findings.metric: P(stop | previous two games both lost); P(stop | after WW) = 0.143 [0.123, 0.160]
findings.caveat: The stopping hazard is roughly flat by game number: after a win it stays between 0.09 and 0.21, after a loss between 0.30 and 0.43.

findings.claim: The last game of a session scores 0.199 points less than the other games, and 0.183 less relative to the model's pre-game expectation, largely because a loss is what makes the player stop.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, last game of the session minus the other games (raw score difference: -0.199 [-0.226, -0.172])
findings.caveat: Part of this is the stopping rule itself (a loss makes the player stop), so the fatigue sections exclude last games or compare within equal-length sessions.

findings.claim: In the last game of a session the player loses slightly more expected points per move than in other games while the opponents lose slightly less, neither difference clearly non-zero.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, last game of the session minus the other games, player and opponents
findings.caveat: Confounded with the stopping rule: the last game is the one lost.

findings.claim: Game 2 of a session is not played differently from game 1 of the same session, and the opponents' change is the same, so there is no warm-up effect.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, game 2 minus game 1 of the same session, non-last games only, paired per session (score minus model expectation: -0.013 [-0.051, 0.032])
findings.caveat: Only sessions that went on to at least game 3, so neither game is the one stopped after.

findings.claim: In bullet, game 10 or later of a session differs from game 1 of the same session by 0.0064 ep per move for the player and 0.0056 for the opponents, neither distinguishable from zero.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, game 10+ minus game 1 of the same session, non-last games only, paired per session
findings.caveat: Continuing after game 8 is a stronger selection on going well than continuing after game 1, which biases late non-last games slightly in the player's favour; treat small negative late differences as 'no fatigue', not improvement.

findings.claim: In bullet, the result of game 10 or later relative to the model's expectation is no different from game 1 of the same session.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, game 10+ minus game 1 of the same session, non-last games only (naive curve: +0.014 in game 1 to +0.047 in game 10+)
findings.caveat: The naive curve's rise with game number is selection (long sessions are the ones that went well); the paired, non-last comparison removes it.

findings.claim: In bullet, games 7-9 of a session lose 11 cp per move less than game 1 of the same session, the only corrected-A move-quality cell whose interval excludes zero, and in the direction of better late play.
findings.metric: cp lost per move, games 7-9 minus game 1 of the same session, non-last games only (ep per move: 0.0007 [-0.0064, 0.0070])
findings.caveat: cp_loss is the secondary measure; the ep per move cell for the same games is flat, and late non-last games are selected towards sessions that went well.

findings.claim: In blitz, games 7-9 of a session are not played worse than game 1 of the same session.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, games 7-9 minus game 1 of the same session, non-last games only (score minus model expectation: -0.030 [-0.215, 0.162])
findings.caveat: Few blitz sessions reach 7 games; the 10+ cell is blank (13 sessions).

findings.claim: In rapid, game 5 of a session is not played worse than game 1 of the same session.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, game 5 minus game 1 of the same session, non-last games only (score minus model expectation: -0.060 [-0.261, 0.142])
findings.caveat: Rapid late-session cells are small and mostly blank (fewer than 20 sessions from game 6 on).

findings.claim: Game 6 of a session has about one fewer move losing at least 0.2 ep per 100 moves than game 1 of the same session; no corrected cell in any time class shows the player clearly worse than in game 1.
findings.metric: moves losing >= 0.2 ep per 100 moves, game 6 minus game 1 of the same session, non-last games only (ep per move: -0.0014 [-0.0067, 0.0036])
findings.caveat: Late non-last games are selected towards sessions that went well; the report says to read small negative late differences as 'no fatigue', not improvement.

findings.claim: Within sessions of exactly 4 games the player loses more ep per move than the opponents only in the last game (the one stopped after); in every earlier position the player-minus-opponents gap is near zero.
findings.metric: ep lost per move in game 4 of 4-game sessions, player and opponents, with the paired player-minus-opponents difference
findings.caveat: The last game is the one the player stopped after, so this is the stop effect, not fatigue; the opponents' curve follows the player's position by position (the 'your - their' column stays near zero elsewhere).

findings.claim: Bullet games played 60-120 minutes into a session are not played worse than the pool average, and the opponents' error rate in those games is the same.
findings.metric: ep lost per move in games starting 60-120 minutes after the session's first game, naive view, player and opponents
findings.caveat: Only 4% of sessions last 60 minutes or more, so the corrected columns (non-last games of sessions lasting at least 60 minutes) are thin.

findings.claim: Pooled across sessions, each doubling of the game number adds 0.044 points relative to the model's expectation, but within sessions the slope is -0.002: the pooled gain is selection (long sessions are the ones that went well).
findings.metric: OLS coefficient on log2(game number) for score minus model expectation, pooled regression on non-last games of multi-game sessions (within-session, demeaned: -0.002 [-0.024, 0.024])
findings.unit: points per game per doubling of game number
findings.caveat: Pooled compares games across sessions as well as within them, so a long session that went well contributes many late, good games (the stopping rule again).

findings.claim: Within sessions, a doubling of the game number changes the player's ep per move by -0.0010 and the gap to the opponents by -0.0002, neither distinguishable from zero.
findings.metric: session-demeaned OLS coefficient on log2(game number) for ep lost per move (player, opponents, and player-minus-opponents per game), non-last games of multi-game sessions, fatigue and minutes estimated together
findings.unit: ep per move per doubling of game number
findings.caveat: Previous-result terms are left out of the within model because a demeaned lagged outcome in panels of 2-10 games is badly biased.

findings.claim: Within sessions, each additional 30 minutes of play changes the player's ep per move by 0.0023 and the opponents' by 0.0022, so the gap between them does not move with time played.
findings.metric: session-demeaned OLS coefficient on minutes/30 for ep lost per move (player, opponents, player-minus-opponents), non-last games of multi-game sessions
findings.caveat: Score minus model expectation per 30 minutes within sessions is -0.029 [-0.089, 0.026].

findings.claim: With game number and minutes held fixed, a lost previous game is followed by a score 0.058 below the model's expectation and a player-minus-opponents ep gap 0.0018 wider than after a drawn previous game or the first game.
findings.metric: pooled OLS coefficient on 'previous game lost' for the player-minus-opponents ep per move (score minus model expectation: -0.058 [-0.098, -0.010]; player ep: 0.0029 [-0.0001, 0.0061]; opponents ep: 0.0012 [-0.0019, 0.0041]); reference: previous game drawn or first game of the session
findings.caveat: The 'previous game won' coefficient is -0.012 [-0.055, 0.028] for score and 0.0002 [-0.0011, 0.0017] for the ep gap; year dummies not shown.

findings.section: all: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: The game after a loss scores 0.055 points less relative to the model's expectation than the game after a win, the one real within-session signal in the data.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation (move-1 calibration model, knows both pre-game ratings), next game after a loss minus after a win; after a loss: -0.014 [-0.035, 0.006], after a win: 0.041 [0.019, 0.061]; score minus Elo expectation: -0.053 [-0.083, -0.025]
findings.n: 4307 games (2457 after a win, 1850 after a loss)
findings.stake_note: The loss-minus-win contrast in score minus model expectation for the next game; the report does not price a stopping rule beyond this contrast, and it is an upper bound on what pausing after a loss could recover in the 1850 post-loss games.
findings.caveat: Measured on the games the player chose to play after a loss; a common cause (a bad day, a stronger pool at that hour) can produce autocorrelation that looks like tilt. The opponents' numbers in the same games are the control for the pool.

findings.section: all: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: After a loss the player loses 0.0024 more ep per move than after a win, but the opponents in those games also lose 0.0017 more, so the player's own gap to the opponents widens by only 0.0007.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, game after a loss minus game after a win, player and opponents, with the paired player-minus-opponents difference
findings.caveat: Tilt is about results more than moves: the opponents' error rate rises almost as much, which points at the kind of game (pool, pace) rather than the player's play.

findings.section: all: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: After a loss the player makes 0.27 more moves losing at least 0.2 ep per 100 moves, and loses 2.8 cp per move more, than after a win.
findings.metric: moves losing >= 0.2 ep per 100 moves, game after a loss minus game after a win (cp lost per move: 2.8 [0.3, 5.4])
findings.caveat: Intervals barely exclude zero.

findings.section: all: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: A larger share of the losses that follow a loss end by resignation than of the losses that follow a win (0.300 vs 0.217).
findings.metric: resignations as a share of the player's losses, game after a loss minus game after a win; after a loss 0.300 [0.270, 0.334], after a win 0.217 [0.192, 0.241]

findings.section: all: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: The share of games lost on time is not clearly higher after a loss than after a win.
findings.metric: share of games the player lost on time, game after a loss minus game after a win (after a loss 0.177 [0.160, 0.194], after a win 0.160 [0.145, 0.177])

findings.section: all: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: After a loss the player spends 0.16 s more per move than after a win while the opponents' pace does not change; the slowdown is clear in bullet (0.10 s) and blitz (0.38 s).
findings.metric: player's seconds per move, game after a loss minus game after a win, with the opponents' change in the same games (bullet 0.10 [0.03, 0.16], blitz 0.38 [0.12, 0.67], rapid 0.31 [-0.41, 1.09])
findings.caveat: Pooled across time classes the interval includes zero; the per-class contrasts in bullet and blitz exclude it.

findings.section: bullet: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: In bullet the game after a loss scores 0.052 points less relative to the model's expectation than the game after a win.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, next game after a loss minus after a win (after a loss -0.022 [-0.051, 0.007], after a win 0.030 [0.004, 0.058])
findings.n: 2667 games (1517 after a win, 1150 after a loss)
findings.stake_note: Loss-minus-win contrast in the next game's score relative to the model; an upper bound on what avoiding post-loss games could recover.
findings.caveat: Games the player chose to play after a loss; CIs bootstrapped over sessions.

findings.section: bullet: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: In bullet the player loses 0.0028 more ep per move after a loss than after a win, the opponents 0.0022 more, and the gap between them widens by 0.0006, not clearly non-zero.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, game after a loss minus game after a win, player and opponents, with the paired difference

findings.section: blitz: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: In blitz the game after a loss scores 0.047 points less relative to the model's expectation than the game after a win.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, next game after a loss minus after a win (after a loss 0.003 [-0.030, 0.040], after a win 0.050 [0.019, 0.081])
findings.n: 1270 games (717 after a win, 553 after a loss)
findings.stake_note: Loss-minus-win contrast in the next game's score relative to the model; an upper bound on what avoiding post-loss games could recover.
findings.caveat: The Elo-expectation version is -0.042 [-0.091, 0.004], just including zero.

findings.section: blitz: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: In blitz the player's move quality after a loss is not measurably different from after a win, for the player or the opponents.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, game after a loss minus game after a win, player and opponents, with the paired difference

findings.section: rapid: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: In rapid the game after a loss scores 0.106 points less relative to the model's expectation than the game after a win, with the interval reaching zero.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, next game after a loss minus after a win (after a loss -0.018 [-0.092, 0.068], after a win 0.088 [0.036, 0.141])
findings.n: 370 games (223 after a win, 147 after a loss)
findings.stake_note: Loss-minus-win contrast in the next game's score relative to the model; an upper bound on what avoiding post-loss games could recover.
findings.caveat: Small sample; the Elo-expectation version is -0.100 [-0.202, 0.013].

findings.section: rapid: by the previous game's result
findings.claim: In rapid the player's and the opponents' move quality after a loss is not measurably different from after a win.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, game after a loss minus game after a win, player and opponents, with the paired difference

findings.section: By the losing streak before the game
findings.claim: After three or more losses in a row the next game scores 0.084 points less relative to the model's expectation than after a win or draw (-0.045 vs 0.039).
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, games after 3+ consecutive losses minus games after 0 (previous game won or drawn); after 3+: -0.045 [-0.107, 0.017], after 0: 0.039 [0.020, 0.059]
findings.stake_note: Score deficit after 3+ losses versus none in the next game; only 177 games follow a 3+ streak, so the total at stake is small.
findings.caveat: Not a dose-response: relative to none the deficit is -0.046 [-0.075, -0.015] after one loss and -0.084 [-0.154, -0.020] after 3+, and 3+ vs 1 directly is -0.038 [-0.101, 0.034], within noise.

findings.section: What this means for the player
findings.claim: The step from one loss to three or more losses in a row before a game is within noise, so the resolved tilt signal is 'after a loss vs after a win', not a dose-response in streak length.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, games after 3+ consecutive losses minus games after exactly 1 loss (after one loss relative to none: -0.046 [-0.075, -0.015])
findings.caveat: The player already stops more often after two losses than after one (section 2), which thins the long-streak sample.

findings.section: By the losing streak before the game
findings.claim: After three or more losses in a row the player's move quality is no different from after a win or draw, and neither is the opponents'.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, games after 3+ consecutive losses minus games after 0, player and opponents, with the paired difference
findings.caveat: Lost on time after 3+ losses vs none: 0.037 [-0.022, 0.100].

findings.claim: Two losses before a game (LL) look worse than a win then a loss (WL), but the contrast does not exclude zero, so the data cannot separate 'the last result' from 'several-game form'.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, games 3+ of a session, previous two results LL minus WL (draws dropped); LL: -0.029 [-0.067, 0.009], WL: -0.001 [-0.033, 0.033], WW: 0.068 [0.038, 0.094], LW: 0.003 [-0.028, 0.038]
findings.caveat: ep per move LL minus WL: -0.0002 [-0.0039, 0.0031] for the player, -0.0006 [-0.0039, 0.0026] for the opponents.

findings.section: By the winning streak before the game
findings.claim: After three or more wins in a row the next game scores 0.093 points above the model's expectation relative to games after no win.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, games after 3+ consecutive wins minus games after 0 wins (after 3+: 0.081 [0.041, 0.118], after 0: -0.011 [-0.032, 0.007])
findings.caveat: The mirror image of the loss effect; games after a winning streak exist only because the player kept playing while winning (the stopping rule).

findings.section: By the winning streak before the game
findings.claim: After three or more wins in a row the player's ep gap to the opponents is 0.0012 per move in the player's favour relative to games after no win, driven by the opponents' errors as much as the player's.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, games after 3+ consecutive wins minus games after 0 wins, player and opponents, with the paired player-minus-opponents difference
findings.caveat: Moves losing >= 0.2 ep per 100: -0.39 [-0.77, -0.03]; selected on the player having kept playing while winning.

findings.section: By how the previous game was lost
findings.claim: A loss that came after the player had been winning (P(win) >= 0.8) is not followed by a worse game than an ordinary loss.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, game after a blown win minus game after an ordinary loss (blown win: 0.030 [-0.046, 0.114], ordinary loss: -0.017 [-0.039, 0.005])
findings.n: 1850 games (123 after a blown win, 1727 after an ordinary loss)
findings.caveat: Only 123 blown wins; ep per move difference -0.0011 [-0.0056, 0.0043].

findings.section: By how the previous game was lost
findings.claim: After a loss on time, the player loses the next game on time a quarter of the time, against 0.154 after being checkmated and 0.116 after resigning; move quality after the three kinds of loss is the same.
findings.metric: share of next games the player lost on time, among games following a loss by timeout (checkmated: 0.154 [0.127, 0.183], resigned: 0.116 [0.089, 0.144]); score minus model expectation after a timeout loss: -0.017 [-0.053, 0.019]
findings.caveat: Largely a time-class composition effect: timeouts cluster in bullet, where losses on time are common in every game.

findings.section: How fast you start the next game
findings.claim: The player starts the next game within 30 seconds 77% of the time after a loss and 81% after a win; the median gap is 8 s after a loss and 7 s after a win.
findings.metric: share of next games started within 30 s of the previous game's end, after a loss (after a win: 0.81 [0.79, 0.83]; after a draw: 0.79 [0.73, 0.84])

findings.claim: Games that make up a one-game session score 0.091 points below the model's expectation, while games in sessions of 11 or more score 0.090 above it.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation for games in sessions of exactly 1 game (sessions of 11+: 0.090 [0.067, 0.116]; excluding the last game of 11+ sessions: 0.105 [0.083, 0.129])
findings.caveat: Descriptive: short sessions are short partly because they went badly (section 2); long sessions gain because the player keeps playing while winning and stops when losing, not because long sessions make the player play better.

findings.claim: In sessions of 11 or more games the player loses fewer ep per move than the opponents, but by a margin within the intervals.
findings.metric: ep lost per move in games of sessions with 11+ games, player and opponents (excluding the last game: 0.0288 [0.0271, 0.0306] vs 0.0304 [0.0287, 0.0322])
findings.caveat: Selected: sessions are long because they went well.

findings.claim: Sessions of 11 or more rated games gain 25.3 rating points on average and end above where they started 73% of the time; one-game sessions lose 1.6 points on average and gain rating 38% of the time.
findings.metric: mean summed rating change per session, sessions of 11+ rated games (P(session gained rating) = 0.733 [0.620, 0.834]; one-game sessions: -1.6 [-2.5, -0.8] and 0.380 [0.335, 0.430])
findings.n: 75 sessions of 11+ rated games (392 one-game sessions)
findings.caveat: Long sessions gain rating because the player keeps playing while winning and stops when losing (section 2), not because long sessions make the player play better.

findings.section: Is there a game number after which play is worse?
findings.claim: Non-last games after game 3 score 0.041 points less relative to the model's expectation than games 1-3 of the same sessions, with no change in move quality, so a fixed 'stop after N games' rule is not supported.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, non-last games numbered 4+ minus non-last games 1-3 in the same sessions (sessions reaching at least 5 games), paired per session; player ep per move: -0.0002 [-0.0028, 0.0027], opponents: -0.0006 [-0.0030, 0.0018]
findings.caveat: The other N give -0.030 [-0.063, 0.002] (N=2), -0.021 [-0.060, 0.018] (N=4), 0.022 [-0.025, 0.070] (N=6) and -0.092 [-0.175, -0.008] (N=10, 63 sessions); no N shows worse move quality, so the report attributes the score dips to the previous result rather than the game number.

findings.section: Is there a game number after which play is worse?
findings.claim: Move quality in non-last games after game 3 is identical to games 1-3 of the same sessions, for the player and the opponents.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, non-last games numbered 4+ minus non-last games 1-3 in the same sessions, paired per session, player and opponents
findings.caveat: For N=10 the player's ep difference is 0.0009 [-0.0048, 0.0065] (63 sessions).

findings.claim: The tilt contrast is the same whether sessions are cut at a 15, 30 or 60-minute gap.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, game after a loss minus game after a win, with the session gap set to 15 minutes (30 min: -0.055 [-0.084, -0.028]; 60 min: -0.054 [-0.082, -0.024])
findings.n: 1638 sessions (15-minute gap), 5572 games in multi-game sessions

findings.claim: The fatigue contrast (games 5+ vs game 1 of the same session) stays indistinguishable from zero for both sides under a 60-minute session gap, as under 15 and 30 minutes.
findings.metric: ep lost per move, corrected A, games 5+ minus game 1 of the same session, with the session gap set to 60 minutes, player and opponents (30 min: 0.0014 [-0.0026, 0.0053] vs 0.0022 [-0.0021, 0.0061]; 15 min: 0.0019 [-0.0023, 0.0056] vs 0.0021 [-0.0017, 0.0058])
findings.n: 1288 sessions (60-minute gap), 5737 games in multi-game sessions
findings.caveat: P(stop | loss) - P(stop | win) shrinks from 0.169 [0.150, 0.193] at 15 min to 0.127 [0.108, 0.148] at 60 min, as expected when longer pauses no longer end a session.
